quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Why crossing guards use bright flags to help children cross busy streets"?
quests.question: Why crossing guards use bright flags to help children cross busy streets
quests.hint: Think about when children are usually walking to and from school.
quests.explanation: Yes! Crossing guards help children safely cross streets during school hours, in the day.
quests.funFact: Bright colors like orange and yellow are used because they're easiest for drivers to spot!

quests.instruction: "Why cyclists add reflective strips to their bikes before riding home late" — when does this happen?
quests.question: Why cyclists add reflective strips to their bikes before riding home late
quests.hint: Think about when reflective strips would actually help a cyclist be seen.
quests.explanation: Yes! Reflective strips help cyclists be seen once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: Reflective materials bounce light straight back toward its source, making them extra visible!

quests.instruction: "Why cyclists wear helmets before riding to school" — when does this happen?
quests.question: Why cyclists wear helmets before riding to school
quests.hint: Think about when children usually ride their bikes to get to school.
quests.explanation: Yes! Riding to school happens in the morning, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: A properly fitted helmet can help protect your head in case of a fall!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Why drivers switch on their headlights once it's hard to see the road"?
quests.question: Why drivers switch on their headlights once it's hard to see the road
quests.hint: Think about when it actually becomes hard to see the road without help.
quests.explanation: Yes! Headlights are needed once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: Headlights help drivers see the road ahead and help other cars see them too!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Why lifeguards blow a whistle when someone swims too far out". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.question: Why lifeguards blow a whistle when someone swims too far out
quests.hint: Think about when public pools and beaches are usually open with lifeguards on duty.
quests.explanation: Yes! Lifeguards are usually on duty watching swimmers during the day.
quests.funFact: Lifeguards watch the water constantly, scanning for anyone who needs help!

quests.instruction: "Why campers keep a flashlight close inside their tent" — when does this happen?
quests.question: Why campers keep a flashlight close inside their tent
quests.hint: Think about when a flashlight would actually be needed inside a tent.
quests.explanation: Yes! Flashlights are needed once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: A flashlight is one of the most important things to pack for a safe camping trip!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Why a construction site puts up bright orange cones around new sidewalks"?
quests.question: Why a construction site puts up bright orange cones around new sidewalks
quests.hint: Think about when construction crews are usually working outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! Construction work is usually done during the day.
quests.funFact: Bright orange cones are used because that color stands out against almost any background!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Why houses use motion-sensor lights near the front door". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.question: Why houses use motion-sensor lights near the front door
quests.hint: Think about when a motion-sensor light would actually need to switch on to help you see.
quests.explanation: Yes! Motion-sensor lights are most useful once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: These clever lights use a sensor to detect movement and switch on automatically!

quests.instruction: "Why a school bus has flashing lights to warn cars to stop" — when does this happen?
quests.question: Why a school bus has flashing lights to warn cars to stop
quests.hint: Think about when school buses are usually picking up and dropping off students.
quests.explanation: Yes! School buses run their routes during school hours, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: These flashing lights warn drivers that children may be crossing nearby!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Why runners choose reflective vests for an evening jog"?
quests.question: Why runners choose reflective vests for an evening jog
quests.hint: Think about when the daylight starts fading during a run.
quests.explanation: Yes! Evening leads into night, when reflective vests help runners stay visible.
quests.funFact: Reflective vests can make a runner visible to drivers from hundreds of feet away!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A science class learning that the moon can sometimes be seen even while the sun is still up". What time of day is it?
quests.question: A science class learning that the moon can sometimes be seen even while the sun is still up
quests.hint: Think about when a science class is usually meeting to learn something new.
quests.explanation: Yes! Science class meets during school hours, in the daytime — even when the lesson is about the moon!
quests.funFact: The moon really can be seen in a bright daytime sky, especially in the early morning or late afternoon!

quests.instruction: "A round, glowing moon hanging high in a star-filled sky" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A round, glowing moon hanging high in a star-filled sky
quests.hint: Think about when the moon and stars are actually visible together like this.
quests.explanation: Yes! A full, round moon is visible at night.
quests.funFact: This fully round moon is called a full moon, and it happens about once a month!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An astronomer reviewing yesterday's late photos on a bright morning"?
quests.question: An astronomer reviewing yesterday's late photos on a bright morning
quests.hint: Think about what time scientists usually review their notes and data.
quests.explanation: Yes! Morning is part of the daytime, even if the astronomer is looking at nighttime photos.
quests.funFact: Astronomers often study their photos and data during the day, after a long night of observing!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A stargazer noting that the moon looks like a thin sliver tonight, almost gone"?
quests.question: A stargazer noting that the moon looks like a thin sliver tonight, almost gone
quests.hint: Think about when a stargazer would actually be outside, looking up at the moon.
quests.explanation: Yes! Stargazing happens at night, when the moon and stars are visible.
quests.funFact: This thin sliver shape is called a crescent moon!

quests.instruction: "A farmers market packing up its final stalls as shoppers browse one more time" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A farmers market packing up its final stalls as shoppers browse one more time
quests.hint: Think about when farmers markets are usually open before they close for the day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Farmers markets are open during the day, even in their final hour before packing up.
quests.funFact: Farmers markets often sell produce picked just hours before the market opens!

quests.instruction: "A farmers market's empty stalls, tarps pulled over unsold vegetables" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A farmers market's empty stalls, tarps pulled over unsold vegetables
quests.hint: Think about when a farmers market would finally be closed, with tarps covering everything.
quests.explanation: Yes! A closed, covered market suggests it's after hours, at night.
quests.funFact: Covering unsold produce helps protect it until the market opens again!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A dog park filled with pups chasing balls and owners chatting on benches". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.question: A dog park filled with pups chasing balls and owners chatting on benches
quests.hint: Think about when dog parks are usually busiest with visitors.
quests.explanation: Yes! Dog parks are usually busiest with visitors during the day.
quests.funFact: Dog parks give pets a safe space to run, play, and socialize with other dogs!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A dog park gate locked, its fields empty and still"?
quests.question: A dog park gate locked, its fields empty and still
quests.hint: Think about when a busy dog park would finally be locked up and empty.
quests.explanation: Yes! A locked, empty dog park suggests it's closed for the night.
quests.funFact: Many public parks have set hours and are locked up once it gets dark!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A crossing signal counting down seconds as pedestrians hurry across"?
quests.question: A crossing signal counting down seconds as pedestrians hurry across
quests.hint: Think about when city streets are usually busiest with walking pedestrians.
quests.explanation: Yes! City streets are usually busiest with pedestrians during the day.
quests.funFact: These countdown signals help pedestrians know exactly how much time they have to cross safely!

quests.instruction: "A crossing signal blinking uselessly over a street with no cars in sight" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A crossing signal blinking uselessly over a street with no cars in sight
quests.hint: Think about when a usually busy street would have no cars at all.
quests.explanation: Yes! An empty street with no cars suggests it's very late at night.
quests.funFact: Some traffic signals switch to a simple blinking pattern late at night when streets are quiet!

quests.instruction: "A food truck's line stretching around the corner during a lunch rush" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A food truck's line stretching around the corner during a lunch rush
quests.hint: Think about when lunchtime usually happens.
quests.explanation: Yes! A lunch rush happens in the middle of the day.
quests.funFact: Food trucks can serve hundreds of hungry customers during a busy lunch hour!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A food truck parked and dark, its window shutter pulled down tight"?
quests.question: A food truck parked and dark, its window shutter pulled down tight
quests.hint: Think about when a food truck would be closed up and dark for the day.
quests.explanation: Yes! A closed, dark food truck suggests it's done serving for the night.
quests.funFact: Food trucks often park in the same safe spot every night after their shift ends!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A recycling truck's mechanical arm lifting a bin high overhead"?
quests.question: A recycling truck's mechanical arm lifting a bin high overhead
quests.hint: Think about when garbage and recycling trucks usually make their rounds.
quests.explanation: Yes! Recycling and garbage collection usually happen during the day.
quests.funFact: Some recycling trucks can lift and empty a bin in just a few seconds!

quests.instruction: "A recycling bin sitting untouched at the curb until morning pickup" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A recycling bin sitting untouched at the curb until morning pickup
quests.hint: Think about when a bin would be sitting out, waiting for the next morning.
quests.explanation: Yes! A bin waiting overnight for morning pickup suggests it's currently nighttime.
quests.funFact: Many neighborhoods have recycling picked up on the very same day every week!

quests.instruction: "A city park fountain misting joggers as they pass by" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A city park fountain misting joggers as they pass by
quests.hint: Think about when city parks are usually busiest with joggers.
quests.explanation: Yes! City parks are usually busiest with joggers and walkers during the day.
quests.funFact: A cool misty fountain is a favorite way for joggers to beat the heat!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A city park fountain switched off, its basin catching only moonlight"?
quests.question: A city park fountain switched off, its basin catching only moonlight
quests.hint: Think about the word 'moonlight' — when does that actually shine?
quests.explanation: Yes! Moonlight only shines at night.
quests.funFact: Some park fountains are switched off overnight to help save water and electricity!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A school nurse checking a temperature before sending a student back to class". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.question: A school nurse checking a temperature before sending a student back to class
quests.hint: Think about when the school nurse's office is usually open.
quests.explanation: Yes! The school nurse's office is open during school hours, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: School nurses help take care of students who feel sick or get hurt during the school day!

quests.instruction: "A school nurse's office locked up, its light finally switched off" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A school nurse's office locked up, its light finally switched off
quests.hint: Think about when the school nurse's office would finally be locked up and dark.
quests.explanation: Yes! A locked, dark office suggests school has ended for the day and night has come.
quests.funFact: School offices are locked up every evening to keep supplies and records safe!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A crowd forming outside a bakery before the doors even open"?
quests.question: A crowd forming outside a bakery before the doors even open
quests.hint: Think about when a bakery would be about to open for the morning.
quests.explanation: Yes! A crowd waiting for a bakery to open suggests it's early morning, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Some bakeries sell out of their most popular treats within the very first hour of opening!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A bakery's 'closed' sign swinging gently in the evening breeze"?
quests.question: A bakery's 'closed' sign swinging gently in the evening breeze
quests.hint: Think about when a bakery would already be closed up for the night.
quests.explanation: Yes! Evening leads into night, when a bakery has closed for the day.
quests.funFact: Many bakeries close in the evening and start baking fresh again very early the next day!
